- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) and forecast is trending down, adjust downward bias by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows sharp declines followed by sentiment spikes, model tends to overshoot recovery — reduce forecast peak by 3–8% in next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20) and forecast is rising, cap upward momentum at 1–3% above recent high to avoid overbought bias.  
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above true outcome, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% from next forecast unless sentiment is strong positive.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 10% of forecast range, reduce forecast by 5–10% to reflect underestimation bias.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings (e.g., -0.10 to 0.06), model tends to lag — add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
